text:
incident-bot: P1 alert — Dedicated pool eu-west-2-ded-42 showing sustained p99 > 10s for streaming/generate endpoints. queue_depth = 1.2k, warmup_misses spiked, streaming stalls flagged. Paging @jamal_oncall :rotating_light:

jamal_oncall: on it. seeing the same in graphs. which tenants impacted? any error rates up?

kevin_support: getting CS reports — 3 customers reported timeouts and stalled streams, one on prod critical path. support ticket numbers: #8421, #8424, #8427.

maria_sre: quick triage — check autoscale events and warmup log markers. if autoscaler increased desired but warmup didn't finish, we likely have cold GPU warmups starving the dispatcher.

devin_runtime: pulling runtime logs now. tail excerpt: ```
[2026-03-14T10:02:12Z] pool=eu-west-2-ded-42 accept=120 tokens/sec queue=1187 warmup_miss=true
[2026-03-14T10:02:15Z] kv_cache_miss=0.87 stall_detected=true stream_chunk_delay=250ms
[2026-03-14T10:03:01Z] autoscaler_trigger desired=24 -> 36 reason=burst
[2026-03-14T10:03:45Z] node_ready=false warmup_in_progress=true
```

devin_runtime: autoscaler did request nodes but warmup_in_progress kept them non-ready; headroom was zero so dispatcher kept queueing to existing hot nodes.

jamal_oncall: status — are there free nodes we can hot-attach or a fast fallback model we can switch traffic to?

maria_sre: two immediate mitigations: 1) scale pool manually with pre-warmed template (force-ready nodes), 2) route new streaming traffic to fallback model (smaller quantized model) to reduce per-req GPU time. I'd do both in parallel.

devin_runtime: I can spin up prewarmed instances using the prewarm image (runtimectl). Command: ```
# manual fast path
runtimectl pool scale eu-west-2-ded-42 --instances 48 --force-prewarm
```
This should flip nodes to ready state ~5-7min.

jamal_oncall: doing manual scale now. running the command.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: manual scale job queued (job-id: ms-2039991111-1). ETA ~6m.

kevin_support: drafting customer-facing note. Proposed short blurb: "We're investigating increased latency affecting streaming responses. We're routing new requests to an alternate model and scaling capacity. We'll follow up with timeline and mitigations." Thoughts?

olivia_prodeng: include whether there's data leakage or error responses — say "no evidence of data loss" if true. keep it concise.

jamal_oncall: we should also reduce batch window and lower max concurrent per-stream on the hot nodes to reduce tail blocking. Will push config change: ```
# reduce batching to mitigate p99
runtimectl config set eu-west-2-ded-42 --streaming_max_concurrency=8 --batch_window_ms=10
```
Applying now.

devin_runtime: batch config updated. Observability note: enable streaming-stall traces. ```
tracectl enable --tag streaming-stall --pool eu-west-2-ded-42
```

customer-ops-bot: notif: Customers A, B, C (IDs redacted) currently experiencing degraded streaming. Notifying account reps.

maria_sre: we should consider short-circuiting long-running queued requests — convert queued streaming to sync fallback with shorter token limits so clients get a response. Add mapping rule: if queued_time > 10s then route to fallback_small and mark as degraded.

jamal_oncall: implementing queued-time rule in router. ```
# router rule
if request.queued_ms > 10000 then route -> model:rdw-fallback-small@v2 tag=degraded
```
Rule pushed.

devin_runtime: after scale job completed, some nodes still warmup_in_progress; however ready count + fallback routing reduced queue from 1.2k -> 300 in 9m. p95 improved slowly, p99 still high due to a few long-running streams.

kevin_support: sending update to customers: "We're scaling capacity and routing traffic to a fallback model to restore responsiveness; some streaming sessions may show truncated or degraded responses while we stabilize." Sending now.

maria_sre: root-cause hypothesis so far: simultaneous large burst from a few tenants (test harness + real traffic) triggered aggressive scale-up but autoscaler settings expect faster GPU warmup. warmup_miss metric spiked and headroom=0 made dispatcher keep sending to saturated nodes.

jamal_oncall: raising mitigation summary: manual prewarm scale + routing fallback + batch-window reduction + queued-time short-circuit. Observed impact: queue_depth -> 300, p95 ~ 450ms, p99 ~ 2.1s at 18 minutes after mitigation start. Still above target for streaming p99 (target 1.2s) but much improved.

olivia_prodeng: agree we need a customer impact assessment and communications timeline. please capture affected tenant ids and duration of degradation.

kevin_support: collecting list from support tickets and telemetry — will attach to incident doc.

maria_sre: action items (quick): 1) temporary: increase autoscaler warmup timeout & prewarm pool headroom, 2) router: add queued-time short-circuit permanently, 3) runtime: telemetry for warmup_miss as alert, 4) run a soak test of warmup image. Owner suggestions: (1) eng-infra, (2) eng-platform, (3) eng-runtime, (4) eng-ml.

jamal_oncall: handoff: I'm on for next 30m, then handing to maria_sre for follow-up. Leaving notes here. If p99 shoots back up, page maria directly.

maria_sre: ack, I'll take it from jamal. starting a post-incident notes doc and will collect logs.

devin_runtime: logging useful debug snippet for postmortem: ```
# high-latency sample stack
stream_worker:0x12ffa waiting on kv_cache load 1200ms
kernel_init: warmup_step=3/5 elapsed=4100ms
dispatcher: active_sessions=118 dut=0.92
```

incident-bot: incident severity remains P1. Creating incident ticket INC-2039991111 and adding contributors.

kevin_support: final customer update planned in 2 hours after root cause analysis.

maria_sre: preliminary RCA: saturation-driven warmup starvation + zero headroom autoscaler config. Next steps for postmortem: timeline, metrics, a/b of warmup strategies, and an action tracker. I'll author the postmortem.

jamal_oncall: closing on-call note: manual mitigations restored acceptable service for most customers; leaving monitoring alert thresholds tightened. Going offline now — handoff complete. :white_check_mark:

maria_sre: logged follow-up tasks into tracker; will schedule a remediation runbook update and a warmup soak next week. moving this thread to incident doc.

incident-bot: incident state updated -> mitigated."
